talking_points.headline: Family-office succession needs and readiness may diverge
talking_points.context_html: The DBS survey account reports individual-name asset holding, limited trust use and uncertainty about adopting new structures, alongside gaps in continuity planning. For wealth delivery, the implication is that advice and servicing processes may need to distinguish awareness from readiness and make decision authority and continuity arrangements explicit. The article is AI-translated, and the survey results should not be treated as representative of all wealthy families.

talking_points.headline: Succession readiness includes control and governance questions
talking_points.context_html: The DBS survey reports that 43% of families have not involved the next generation in wealth planning and 33% cite a founder’s wish to remain in charge as the main reason for delaying discussions. For private-wealth delivery, this suggests that succession conversations may need to address decision rights and continuity arrangements, not just asset transfer. The findings are survey results and do not establish how prevalent these issues are across the wider wealthy-client population.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Ultra-wealthy families in Asia, including Singapore, lack succession and crisis planning: DBS report Trending in AseanPlusAir Pollutant IndexOthers Also Read
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: A DBS survey of more than 200 family offices reports that 79% of surveyed families want to transfer wealth across at least two generations, while 43% have not involved the next generation in wealth planning. The report also says 33% cite a founder’s desire to remain in charge as the main reason for delaying wealth-transfer discussions, and 54% hold family assets in an individual’s name. For private-wealth delivery, these findings point to succession, governance and continuity as potential client-planning needs; they are survey findings, not a measure of all wealthy families.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: More than half of wealthy families favour holding assets in their own names, risking disputes and estate tax: DBS
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: A DBS report, based on surveys of more than 200 family offices across Asia, Europe and the Middle East, says more than half hold core assets in individuals’ names and only 20% use professionally managed trusts. It also reports that 55% are unsure about introducing new structures in the next 12 months, more than 85% lack comprehensive business-continuity plans, and 47% have yet to use AI or digital tools in daily operations. Public implication: succession, continuity and technology-readiness discussions may need to account for families’ control preferences and implementation barriers; these are survey findings, and the article is identified as AI-translated.

AI & Technology.title: DBS named World's Best Digital Bank
AI & Technology.summary: DBS announced that Global Finance named it World’s Best Digital Bank 2026, the first Asia-headquartered bank to receive that publication’s top global digital banking accolade in its 27-year programme. DBS also retained its corporate/institutional digital-bank title for a third consecutive year and received AI-related awards. The recognition offers a competitor signal about how digital and AI capabilities are being presented in banking, but awards do not establish operational performance or customer outcomes.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Karnataka Bank: Appoints Sughosh Nagendra as New CTO
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Karnataka Bank appointed Sughosh Nagendra as CTO, effective 30 October 2026. The report describes more than 27 years of IT experience spanning technology operations, cybersecurity, cloud computing and transformation, but gives no details of a specific programme. Public implication: this is a technology-leadership change at an Indian bank; the article does not establish what operational or strategic changes will follow.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Deutsche Bank Warns AI Stock Selloff Threatens Dollar Safe-Haven Status
Regulatory & Markets.summary: PYMNTS reports Deutsche Bank strategist George Saravelos’s view that an AI-driven market correction could weaken the dollar’s safe-haven status, alongside reported declines in technology shares and concerns about AI investment returns. Public implication: if AI-related market exposure contributes to broader volatility, wealth teams may face client questions about concentration and currency risk; this is a strategist’s market view relayed through other reporting, not an established forecast or outcome.
